marketing-adds-volume.title: Marketing adds volume
marketing-adds-volume.keywords: clear job, more leads, one stage, first column, the stage must exist
marketing-adds-volume.script: Marketing has a clear job in this picture. It adds volume. It brings more leads into one stage of your pipeline, the first column of the board. A bigger flow of leads helps only if that stage exists and you know where it sits.

defined-entry-point.title: Defined entry point
defined-entry-point.keywords: decide the stage, measure it, webinar or post, forty new names, compare on one board
defined-entry-point.script: That only works if you decide which stage marketing feeds. If you do not, the volume goes in somewhere, but nobody can see where it goes or what it turns into. Give it a defined entry point, and then you can measure it. For example, a webinar or a post might bring in forty new names. If they all land in one column, you can see in a month how many of them became meetings. If they land nowhere, you have forty names and no idea. Marketing and your own outreach can then be compared on the same board.

not-a-substitute.title: Not a substitute
not-a-substitute.keywords: do not wait for marketing, your own first contact, first opportunities, do both, carry the message
not-a-substitute.script: But do not wait for marketing to do your first sales for you. Early on, your own first contact is what opens the first opportunities. Marketing helps it grow. So do both. Make the first calls yourself, learn what works, and then let marketing carry that message to many more people.
